requirements.evidence: All contract routes and views exist and the main flows are implemented: routes/web.php:18-42, app/Livewire/Auth/Login.php, app/Livewire/Auth/Register.php, app/Http/Controllers/PasswordResetController.php, app/Http/Controllers/SessionController.php, app/Http/Controllers/Auth/EmailVerificationController.php. Gaps: resources/views/welcome.blade.php:55 hardcodes visible 'Bulma CSS' text (and bulma-test.blade.php:23 hardcodes '#3273dc'); PasswordResetController.php:22-30 returns a validation error for a malformed/missing e-mail instead of the promised status flash; EmailVerificationController.php:20,27,33 redirects with intended() rather than always to home.

conventions.evidence: Good adherence in places: every view link/action uses route() (e.g. layouts/app.blade.php:19-31), controllers use named redirects (SessionController.php:18, PasswordResetController.php:62), the Livewire components declare #[Layout('layouts.app')] (Login.php:13, Register.php:15), and Password::defaults() is configured once (AppServiceProvider.php:24). Clear deviations: no #[Validate] attributes or rules() method on the Livewire input properties (Login.php:16-27, Register.php:18-42); the reset update validates three fields inline (PasswordResetController.php:43-47) instead of a Form Request; no docs/CHANGELOG updates; no Blade component for the repeated auth field markup; the Bulma navbar has no burger toggle (layouts/app.blade.php:17-35).

security.evidence: No exploitable weakness found: dynamic output uses {{ }} throughout (e.g. home.blade.php:11, login.blade.php:5-10) and there is no {!! !!}; every POST form has @csrf (forgot-password.blade.php:16, reset-password.blade.php:12, verify-email.blade.php:16,24, home.blade.php:13, layouts/app.blade.php:26); login/register regenerate the session (Login.php:41, Register.php:54); logout invalidates the session and regenerates the token (SessionController.php:14-16); rate limits cover login/register/forgot/verification (Login.php:46-57, Register.php:28-36, routes/web.php:23,37,41); the verification link is signed (routes/web.php:37) and validated by EmailVerificationRequest (EmailVerificationController.php:17); mass assignment is limited to name/email/password (Register.php:44-48).

tests.evidence: No test files appear anywhere in change.diff (grep for tests/, Test.php and Pest/PHPUnit files found nothing), so there is no coverage for login, registration, logout, home gating, password reset, e-mail verification, rate limits, the pt-BR/en screens, or the required Livewire unauthorized/tamper paths.

simplicity.evidence: The same label/control/input/@error block is copy-pasted across six views (forgot-password.blade.php:17-25, reset-password.blade.php:14-22, verify-email.blade.php:17-21, livewire/auth/login.blade.php:7-15, livewire/auth/register.blade.php:7-42); the reset controller pre-checks User::where(...)->exists() (PasswordResetController.php:26-28) even though the broker already resolves the user; the two Livewire components duplicate the throttle/error pattern. No speculative abstractions otherwise.

readability.evidence: Small, intention-revealing methods (Login::submit/ensureIsNotRateLimited/throttleKey at Login.php:22-62, SessionController::destroy at SessionController.php:10-19), consistent formatting, no debug output or dead code. Minor noise: the redundant $email ?? request()->query('email') fallback (reset-password.blade.php:17) and the layout mixing @yield('content') with {{ $slot ?? '' }} (layouts/app.blade.php:37-38).

scope.evidence: All production changes serve auth or the required localization; the only unrelated edits are the removal of @fonts and whitespace-only churn in welcome.blade.php (around :7-9) and bulma-test.blade.php.

issues.explanation: No Pest/PHPUnit tests were added for any new auth behavior; the conventions require tests for every feature, including unauthorized-call and tamper tests for Livewire actions, so this change is not done.

The public input properties have no #[Validate] attributes and there is no rules() method; rules are passed inline to $this->validate(), which deviates from the project's Livewire pattern and the non-negotiable Livewire security policy.
The reset update validates three fields (token, e-mail, password) inline with the shared password rule; the conventions call for a Form Request once rules exceed one or two fields or are shared.
The new auth routes and screens are not reflected in the setup/structure docs or CHANGELOG, contrary to the 'keep docs in sync' convention.
The Bulma navbar renders navbar-menu without a burger/is-active toggle, so the nav links are hidden on small screens; the UI conventions call for the few inline lines needed for the burger.

The visible 'Bulma CSS' text (and the '#3273dc' sample at bulma-test.blade.php:23) is still hardcoded, so the 'all screen text comes from translation files' requirement is not fully met; the hardcoded brand also duplicates the text inside ui.welcome.notice.

Validation runs before the status flash, so a missing or malformed e-mail gets a validation error instead of the promised 'always answers with a status flash' behavior; only valid addresses receive the neutral response.
The verification endpoints use redirect()->intended(...); the task specifies redirecting to home, and intended can send a just-verified user to some other previously intended URL.

The User::where(...)->exists() pre-check duplicates the broker's own user lookup; calling Password::sendResetLink() unconditionally and ignoring its status gives the same anti-enumeration behavior with less code.

The same label/control/input/@error markup is copy-pasted across six views instead of an anonymous Blade component, which the Bulma/Blade conventions ask for and which makes the forms harder to keep consistent.

issues.location: resources/views/welcome.blade.php (removal of @fonts, around :7-9); bulma-test.blade.php whitespace hunks
issues.explanation: The @fonts directive removal and trailing-whitespace churn are unrelated to session auth/localization and add review noise.

review.summary: This change implements the full session-auth surface (login/register/logout, home gating, password reset, e-mail verification, and pt-BR/en UI) with solid security basics such as validation, CSRF, session regeneration, rate limiting and signed verification links. It ships zero tests, which the project's TDD and Livewire conventions make a blocker, and it has several convention and localization deviations. The production code is close, but the PR is not approvable until the test suite (including unauthorized and tamper cases) and the noted fixes are added.
